transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-19
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Ava (Redwood AE), Noah (Redwood SE), Priya (CloudScale Head of ML), Liam (Platform), Sofia (Security)

Summary: Short demo/walkthrough of Redwood Console tracing, error analysis, and request logs. Customer concerned about noisy errors, latency spikes, and how to debug production anomalies. Discussed private deployment considerations, access controls, and plan for a short benchmark.

00:00 - Ava: Okay, hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Ava from Redwood, this is Noah, our solutions engineer, we'll run through the Console tracing and error analysis flows, and leave time for Q&A.
00:14 - Priya: Hi thanks, excited. Quick context — we're running prod ML infra on k8s, hybrid across GCP and on-prem for sensitive datasets, and we have some unpredictable latency spikes when we push long context prompts.
00:29 - Noah: Great, that sounds right up the alley. I put together a short deck and I'll demo live in the Console — tracing view, the request logs, and the error analysis. Note: we'll also show how we link traces to raw request payloads and KV cache hits to debug perf.
00:45 - Liam: Quick one — we use a custom auth proxy and SAML for SSO, any blockers for Private?
00:53 - Ava: Not typically; our Private offering supports SAML, KMS integration for keys, and customer-managed networking — we'll share the network diagram after.
01:05 - Noah: Alright pulling up Console now, a couple of caveats: this is a demo tenant so metrics are sampled but the flows are the same. Starting at the Console home -> Observability -> Traces.
01:22 - Noah: So this is the trace list, we index traces by request id, model, latency, and error rate. You can filter by route, model family, and by tags like region or customer-id.
01:34 - Priya: Are those tags automatically captured or do we need to inject them in metadata?
01:39 - Noah: We auto-capture common tags (region, model, route, quantization flag) and you can add custom labels in the SDK header — little snippet shows how to pass x-tenant-id or experiment id.
01:55 - Noah: Clicking into a single trace — timeline view shows the steps: request ingress, tokenization, KV cache lookup, kernel execution, response generation and egress. Each span has timestamps, duration, and logs.
02:12 - Ava: One thing customers like is the KV cache hit/miss visualization — helps explain why some long-history requests are cheaper or faster.
02:20 - Priya: Right, we suspect our cache invalidation may be causing cold starts. Can you correlate cache miss with increased token latency?
02:28 - Noah: Yes, you can overlay cache-hit rate and per-token latency; here I toggle the metric overlay and you can see a cluster of traces where cache misses align with 3x token time.
02:44 - (audio: brief typing)
03:01 - Liam: The trace shows a spike inside the attention kernel, the label says 'attn-compile-optim' — is that a Redwood-internal kernel optimization, or something from the runtime?
03:11 - Noah: That's the runtime selecting a different kernel path due to longer sequence length. We annotate the reason: kernel selection, quantization path, and GPU fallback. Sometimes the kernel change causes a latency bump — the trace notes the trigger.
03:26 - Priya: How about request logs — can we get full request/response payload to repro? We have to be mindful of PII.
03:34 - Ava: By default payloads are redacted in hosted. For Dedicated/Private you can opt-in to retain full payloads, and we support configurable redaction rules; we also integrate with customer KMS for encryption at rest. We'll send the security doc with retention options.
03:52 - Noah: Switching to Request Logs tab — you can search by request id and view raw request headers, model, token counts, and status codes. When a call errors we link to the trace and the error analysis panel.
04:08 - Priya: What sort of errors do you surface? Timeouts, OOM, model rejects?
04:14 - Noah: Yes: timeout, OOM, kernel-failure, rate-limited, and user-level rejections (e.g., policy). Error analysis aggregates top error signatures and shows trends over time.
04:24 - (Priya: okay)
04:32 - Noah: Here's an error signature view — you can click a signature (e.g., OOM in decoder step) to see sample requests and a diff of prompts that triggered it. We also annotate probable root cause: e.g., bad tokenization pattern or unexpected long prefix.
04:49 - Sofia: From a security angle — audit logs, who accessed traces, retention — is that auditable?
04:56 - Ava: Yep, access is tracked. Console has RBAC and per-role views; everything is logged to audit trails, and for Private customers we ship logs to your SIEM. We'll include the audit log sample in the docs.
05:10 - Liam: Can we export traces into our tracing system — say Zipkin or Datadog?
05:16 - Noah: Yes, there are integrations — we can forward trace spans to Datadog/OpenTelemetry collectors and also export CSV/JSON of traces for offline analysis.
05:25 - (short pause)
05:35 - Noah: Now I'll demo a typical debugging flow: we saw an error spike in the last 24 hours, filtering traces by model 'redwood-x' and by region. See this cluster — many have the same error signature.
05:49 - Noah: Clicking into one, the request shows a KV cache miss, then a long kernel compile step, then a 504 at the egress. In the error panel we surface suggestions: warm-up the cache, increase request timeout for that route, or pin a different model variant.
06:06 - Priya: Is there an automated alerting or can we hook an alert to the error signature?
06:12 - Noah: You can create alerts in the Console: e.g., error-rate > 1% for 5 minutes for route /chat. Alerts can trigger webhooks, PagerDuty, or create a ticket.
06:23 - Priya: For on-prem, would that alerting still trigger to our PagerDuty?
06:27 - Ava: Yes, for Private you configure your webhook endpoints inside the control plane. We respect your firewall rules and it's outbound from your network to Redwood control plane unless you opt for fully air-gapped.
06:41 - Liam: A question about performance: can we run a benchmark inside Redwood console with our prompt set?
06:47 - Noah: We have a benchmarking tool — we can run a load test and collect traces, latencies, token costs. For Dedicated we can benchmark pinned capacity. We'll set up a short-run with your prompt set.
06:58 - Priya: Great, we'll share sample prompts after this call.
07:04 - Noah: Moving on — request logs have a 'replay' feature, limited to internal DDL, that lets you replay a request against a different model variant or quantization profile. It's useful to verify fixes without touching prod.
07:20 - Priya: That sounds useful but is the payload kept in Redwood?
07:24 - Ava: Replays use the same retention controls; for Hosted, payloads are short-lived unless you opt-in. For Private you can keep payloads in your VPC. We'll clarify in the appendix.
07:38 - (typing)
07:50 - Noah: Now the Error Analysis dashboard — we show top 10 error signatures, time-to-first-error, and per-model breakdown. You can whitelist certain signatures as benign and suppress alerts.
08:04 - Sofia: If we suppress a sig, can we still see it in raw logs? We don't want to lose data for audits.
08:10 - Noah: Suppression applies to alerting and summary metrics; raw logs and traces remain available per retention policy.
08:18 - Priya: For debugging long tail latency, can you show how to correlate backend GPU metrics to trace durations?
08:25 - Noah: Absolutely — in the trace view you can overlay GPU utilization, memory pressure, and kernel metrics. See this trace where GPU util hits 98% at the same time as token time rises.
08:39 - Liam: Any way to detect bad prompts that cause repeated OOMs?
08:42 - Noah: We have a prompt-diff feature that clusters prompt text patterns; top offending prompts are surfaced and you can tag them for follow-up. It's fuzzy clustering so it handles minor text variations.
08:56 - Priya: How accurate is clustering with noisy transcription? (laugh)
08:59 - Noah: (laugh) We do best-effort, sometimes names are mangled, but clustering focuses on token sequences so it's robust.
09:10 - (brief cross-talk)
09:22 - Ava: I also wanted to point out the 'investigation workspace' — you can bundle a set of traces, notes, and assign to an engineer. Useful for handoffs.
09:35 - Priya: Nice, we already have a bunch of similar incidents.
09:40 - Noah: One more demo: pipeline view — request routing by policy. You can see fallback paths — if dedicated pool is full, requests route to hosted fallback or to a lower-cost quantized variant. Traces record the routing decision with reason codes.
09:58 - Sofia: From security perspective, does routing leak any metadata to hosted fallback?
10:03 - Ava: For most customers we ensure metadata is minimal; however routing to hosted is considered only if customer opts into fallback. We can model a policy that avoids host fallback entirely for sensitive routes.
10:18 - Priya: What about deployment rollout debugging — can we compare traces pre/post rollout?
10:23 - Noah: Yes, you can create a comparison by time window or by rollout tag. The console will diff latency, error rates, and top error signatures between versions.
10:36 - (short pause)
10:45 - Liam: Any limitations on how long traces are stored?
10:49 - Ava: Retention is configurable. Hosted tier has standard retention; Dedicated/Private can extend retention and export to your storage. We'll include pricing for extended retention.
10:59 - Priya: Ok, recap for us: we need the security docs, the network diagram, and an initial benchmark with our prompt set. We'll also want trial access to the Console read-only.
11:12 - Ava: Great — we'll send the docs and spin up a read-only Console invite for Priya and Liam. Noah will coordinate the benchmarking run.
11:22 - (typing)
11:35 - Priya: One last question — do you expose the raw kernel logs so our infra team can correlate JIT/compile events?
11:42 - Noah: We surface kernel decision events in the trace; raw low-level kernel logs can be made available for Dedicated customers on request, subject to support engagement.
11:53 - Ava: Alright, thanks everyone, we'll capture action items. Any final Qs?
11:59 - (Priya: none)
12:04 - Ava: Thanks, we'll follow up with the security appendix and SOC2 artifacts and get that benchmark scheduled.
12:12 - Meeting ends.
